In A, counterexample() gives each entry the 13 has absolutely_minimal, causally_arc_connected, causally_open, causally_open_future, causally_plain, curves_extend, is_causal, locally_causally_open, locally_causally_open_future, locally_push_up, push_up, strongly_causal, strongly_causal_open. The ladder comment at programme/ladder.toml:2530–2534 argued these in words, 'none of which is in Lean'. They are now Lean theorems and conjuncts of Causal.isolatedLine_separates. To write a [[fails]] witness's full form, run ladder.counterexample(d, f) in memory: its `has` is the list of positive conjuncts to state, and its `lacks` the negative ones. Given `have`s of the `from` ids, causal_ladder closes every `has` id on a concrete causality on ℝ, in one call each (T-abs-isolated-line-conjoined).
